title: Care Coordination Guidance — Standing Orders for Recurring RideLink Treatment Trips
content:
Non-Emergency Medical Transportation lets recurring treatment trips be set up once as a standing order on the RideLink levels that allow it. The desk applies the following rule; the qualifying treatments and the longest order are the level's own standing order terms.

**Rule.** Where the level allows standing orders, recurring trips for a treatment among the level's qualifying treatments are set up once as a standing order lasting at most the level's longest order in months, and each leg is booked automatically with the standing order as its booking channel. The treatment schedule is confirmed by the treating provider before the order is set, and the order ends early when the benefit is suspended for a non-exempt purpose or closed.

## Condition — judgement — result

| Condition | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| The level allows standing orders and the treatment qualifies on that level | The recurring trips may be set up as one standing order | Each leg is booked automatically under the order |
| The treating provider has confirmed the treatment schedule | The order may be set | The order lasts no longer than the level's longest order |
| The benefit is suspended for a non-exempt purpose | The order ends early | — |
| The benefit is closed | The order ends early | — |

## Points of judgement

- The provider's confirmation of the schedule comes before the order is set; an order is not set on the member's description of the schedule alone.
- Legs booked under an order show the standing order as their booking channel and carry the standing order's number.
- *Hypothetical:* an order set on 1 January on a level whose longest order is 6 months lasts no longer than 6 months; a further period needs renewal.
